name: PACE-Bench
intro: PACE-Bench 是 PACE 框架为四个昂贵智能体目标物化的代理基准。论文用 14 折留一模型协议验证方法：14 个模型在 19 个低成本非智能体候选基准上的实例得分与目标得分并行形成矩阵，再由局部相关性和全局杠杆度选择每目标 100 个唯一复合实例。公开数据不是留出预测，而是固定超参数后在全部 14 个模型上 fit-all 得到的四份加权代理；19 个候选来源中实际覆盖 12 个。
org: Carnegie Mellon University; Salesforce AI Research
build_method: 目标与来源实例评测, 14折留一模型验证, 局部相关性与全局SVD杠杆度筛选, 全14模型fit-all发布
metric: MAE, Spearman correlation, Pearson correlation, pairwise ranking accuracy, target-evaluation cost
modality: 文本, 代码, 图像
eval_feature: 四个目标专用代理, 每目标100个唯一复合实例, 绝对得分与成对排序预测, 留一验证与fit-all发布分离
scale: 4个目标代理文件：GAIA 100行、SWE Verified 100行、SWE Multimodal 105行、SWT 107行；每份100个唯一复合键；19个候选来源中选中12个；14个模型
build_method_en: Target and Source Instance Evaluation, 14-fold Leave-one-model-out Validation, Local Relevance and Global SVD-leverage Selection, All-14-model Fit-all Release
eval_feature_en: Four Target-specific Proxies, 100 Unique Composite Instances per Target, Absolute-score and Pairwise-ranking Prediction, Separate LOOCV Validation and Fit-all Release
intro_en: PACE-Bench is the materialized proxy benchmark produced by PACE for four expensive agentic targets. The paper validates the method with 14 model-held-out folds: target and source-instance scores from 14 models and 19 low-cost non-agentic candidate benchmarks form parallel matrices, then Local relevance and Global leverage select 100 unique composite instances per target. The public files are not held-out predictions; they are fit-all weighted proxies materialized with fixed hyperparameters on all 14 models and cover 12 of the 19 candidate sources.
scale_en: 4 target proxy files: GAIA 100 rows, SWE Verified 100, SWE Multimodal 105, SWT 107; 100 unique composite keys per file; 12 selected of 19 candidate sources; 14 models
metric_en: MAE, Spearman correlation, Pearson correlation, pairwise ranking accuracy, target-evaluation cost

The pinned official implementation is neulab/pace at commit dc2ef80e00addd519e7d8479f875cc3ecb46c6cb; the materialized selections first appeared at commit 7521a8b737725b6197a3c44b1cd67f1a71e80ad2 and the later pinned commit changes only the PlanBench handler import, not this pipeline. The official dataset is pinned to neulab/pace-bench revision ce177cfe25bc8c8259cadecb56d4db8d9d36ab18; its card hash is c7fbf603d2d6670ff5d43f004e89f83e03c9e29eb62b4c23a13fe9b00c1b1dd4. Dataset hashes are GAIA 80b92f739c5dbadd5a1689df95ebd6a6d8a519656618cf2fad3833cc14fc966e, SWE-Bench Verified 50c85e0d9af3bd601258f2e1f5ff75ca02cc2bb5cd1f1894f89aa7c8dd181559, SWE-Bench Multimodal 8770deea286c155aaefa78b3b3cd77c61e183a7eb6cb3bf6d869b24c9ae4f9ec, and SWT-Bench 9fbb5fb3f3ee358ed72237a06ee7b6848501cf1f08e86d9f2864b737e4e90135. Paper construction facts preserved in the diagrams are 14 configured models; four OpenHands Index targets with GAIA 165, SWE-Bench Multimodal 102, SWE-Bench Verified 500, and SWT-Bench 430 target instances; 19 candidate non-agentic source benchmarks covering 11 capability groups; source and target instance-score matrices; and near-zero-variance filtering. The validation branch is strict model LOOCV in the paper: hold out one model, calibrate selection and regression on the other 13, predict the held-out target, and aggregate 14 predictions. Local ranking is absolute Spearman correlation; Global ranking is SVD leverage h times absolute Spearman; C_L and C_G split the budget, and overlap is replenished in the fixed ratio until the union contains C=100 unique composite source instances. Selection and the Local/Global embeddings precede target-instance bootstrap; the released reproduction uses B=300 and seed=42, and selection itself is not rerun inside bootstrap. Goal A and Goal B share the selected instances. Goal B uses ordered model-score differences and ridge logistic regression. Local and Global predictions are lambda-ensembled. Table 2 reports mean MAE 3.80 percent, Spearman 0.81, Pearson 0.74, pairwise accuracy 84.37 percent, and target-evaluation cost below one percent. Two paper-code boundaries are explicit rather than hidden. First, the paper states that the held-out model is excluded from the Global SVD, while released cli.py computes Vt_full once from all 14 rows of source-score X before the folds; target labels Y remain training-fold-only, so this is transductive source geometry rather than target-label leakage. Second, the paper describes Goal A conceptually as a raw selected C-vector predictor, while released absolute.py operates on SVD coordinates, forms a Spearman-weighted one-dimensional projection, and fits an intercept OLS with numeric fallbacks. The optional auto-tune path selects q, m, nc_h, and nc_d from aggregated held-out labels, so it is not nested cross-validation. The publication branch is deliberately separate: fixed hyperparameters and all 14 models produce fit-all abs and pair selection files; published selections are not held-out predictions or a fifth evaluation result. The pinned HF snapshot has 100 GAIA rows, 100 SWE Verified rows, 105 SWE Multimodal rows, and 107 SWT rows, while each target has exactly 100 unique keys only when identity is the complete tuple source_benchmark, subdir, instance_id. The extra five Multimodal and seven SWT rows are exact Local/Global duplicate identities. The data card's grouping by instance_id, or by instance_id and source_benchmark, is insufficient because identifiers are not globally unique across source and subdirectory. Only 12 of 19 candidate source benchmarks appear in the fit-all release. Content was resolved for 405 of 412 physical rows; seven rows remain null after upstream VisualPuzzles or VisualWebBench drift. HF weight represents the Goal A linear predictor; Goal B weights remain in the repository pair_fit_pinA selection CSV. Openness is bounded: HF declares mixed-upstream and every selected instance retains upstream terms; upstream revisions are not pinned per item; the Git snapshot has neither a LICENSE file nor a tagged release. The flowchart therefore uses primary edges for the two real protocols and dashed secondary edges for fixed evidence, paper-code drift, publication identity, content coverage, and license terms; it does not present generated assets, an audit count, or a fit-all file as final methodological validation. Formal publication evidence [site-a12c-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2055×1113 (English) and 2060×1113 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2053×1111 and 2058×1111. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
